claude.performance_metric: divested mobile-devices business to Lenovo ~$2.91bn at close (~30 months after $12.9bn acquisition); patents retained
claude.rationale: The slice documents a realized fracture at the process/organization interface: upon absorption the entire pre-existing board resigned and senior management (CEO Jha replaced by Woodside, new CFO Wittman) was replaced by acquirer-installed leadership, i.e. the operating organization broke against the acquirer's people/management over the post-deal period (p5_pathway=1). No evidence describes disruption specifically at the product/process interface — there is no standalone audited outcome record and the divestiture facts do not document product-line/operations incoherence — so p4_pathway is uncertain. The slice provides no documented evidence on the controlling-intent archetype or business-model reconciliation, so t1 and t2 are uncertain.

grok.performance_metric: mobile-devices business divested to Lenovo for ~$2.91bn in 2014
grok.rationale: The slice documents Google’s whole-entity acquisition (~$12.9bn, May 2012), board/management replacement at absorption, deregistration, and the 2014 sale of the mobile-devices business to Lenovo (~$2.91bn) with patents retained, but it does not document product-line/operations incoherence over time, so p4_pathway is 0. Management and board replacement is recorded only as an at-closing absorption step, not as a realized process/organization fracture over the 3–5-year horizon, so p5_pathway is 0.
